mention.definition: the continuous movement of water between atmosphere, land, and bodies of water driven by solar energy

mention.name: infiltration
mention.definition: The process of water entering and moving through the ground surface into soil or other porous material.

mention.name: surface runoff
mention.definition: Water flowing over the land surface when precipitation exceeds infiltration capacity or saturation.

mention.name: groundwater recharge
mention.definition: The process by which water enters an aquifer, increasing groundwater storage.

mention.name: groundwater
mention.definition: Water stored in the saturated zone of soil or rock.

mention.name: groundwater storage
mention.definition: The volume of water held within an aquifer or saturated zone.

mention.name: water budget
mention.definition: A quantitative accounting of inputs, outputs, and storage changes in a hydrologic system.

mention.name: groundwater storage
mention.definition: The volume of water held within the saturated zone of an aquifer.

mention.name: surface runoff
mention.definition: Water that flows over the land surface because infiltration capacity is exceeded or saturation occurs.

mention.name: surface runoff
mention.definition: Water flowing over the land surface when infiltration capacity is exceeded or saturation occurs.

mention.name: aquifer
mention.definition: An underground layer of water-bearing permeable rock, rock fractures, or unconsolidated materials (gravel, sand, silt, or clay) from which groundwater can be extracted.

mention.name: watershed
mention.definition: A defined area of land where all precipitation collects and drains into a common outlet, such as a river or lake.
